label: def:hochschild-homology
title: Hochschild homology
html:
Let A be an associative algebra over a commutative ring R, and write A^{e} = A \otimes_R A^{\mathrm{op}} for its enveloping algebra, so that a bimodule over A is the same thing as a left module over A^{e}; A itself is one.

Definition. The Hochschild homology of A is the graded R-module

  HH_{n}(A) \;=\; \operatorname{Tor}^{A^{e}}_{n}(A, A), \qquad n \geq 0 .

It is computed by the Hochschild complex C_{n}(A) = A^{\otimes (n+1)} with the boundary

  b(a_0 \otimes a_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes a_n)
  = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (-1)^{i}\, a_0 \otimes \cdots \otimes a_i a_{i+1} \otimes \cdots \otimes a_n
  \;+\; (-1)^{n}\, a_n a_0 \otimes a_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes a_{n-1},

whose last term wraps the tensor around: it is the cyclic structure of the complex, and the reason its homology deserves the name of a trace. The companion groups HH^{n}(A, M) = \operatorname{Ext}^{n}_{A^{e}}(A, M), for a bimodule M, are the Hochschild cohomology; HH^{n}(A) := HH^{n}(A, A), and it is HH^{2}(A, M) that classifies first-order deformations of the multiplication of A with values in M [weibel1994].

Degree zero. From the complex, HH_{0}(A) = A / [A, A], the quotient of A by the R-span of all commutators ab - ba; this is the cocenter of A. A linear functional \tau \colon A \to R with \tau(ab) = \tau(ba) vanishes on [A, A] and therefore factors through HH_{0}(A). Every trace in this paper — the rigid trace of an endomorphism, the Markov trace on the Hecke algebra, a character of a representation — is a functional of this kind, and every one of them is a function of the Hochschild class alone. This is the whole reason the paper's traces live in degree zero, and it is the part of the definition that the Lean sibling carries: HochschildZero R A is the cocenter, hochschildClass_mul_comm is the identity [ab] = [ba], and traceOnHochschildZero is the factorisation.

Degree one. For A commutative, HH_{1}(A) = \Omega^{1}_{A/R}, the module of Kähler differentials: the class of a_0 \otimes a_1 goes to a_0\, da_1. For A smooth over a field of characteristic zero the pattern continues in every degree, HH_{n}(A) \cong \Omega^{n}_{A/R}; that is the Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg theorem, stated with its hypotheses in a later chapter. For a noncommutative A, such as the quantised coordinate ring of a group at q \neq 1, no such identification is available, and the groups have to be computed [loday-1998].

Two conventions to keep apart. The definition above is for an algebra. For an R-linear category \mathbf{C} the same construction, with the objects of \mathbf{C} in place of the single algebra, gives the Hochschild homology of the category; in degree zero it is the direct sum over objects X of \operatorname{End}(X), modulo the relations fg = gf for every pair of morphisms f \colon X \to Y, g \colon Y \to X. It is this second object, written HH_{0}(\mathbf{C}), that receives the Chern character of the next definitions.
